summary: Eugène Tisserant (1884–1972) worked in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at the Lycée Notre-Dame Saint-Sigisbert, the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1905–1908), and the École du Louvre (~1906–1908).

Eun Hino (born 1981) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a master's course at the University of Tokyo (~2004–2006). He served as a project researcher at the University of Tokyo (~2011–2014) and as an assistant professor at Musashino University (~2014–2017).
Keiun Maeda (1855–1930) was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught Kozui Otani. He served as president of Toyo University and Ryukoku University.

Eun-su Cho (born 1958) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, under Padmanabh S. Jaini, served as an assistant professor at the University of Michigan until 2004, and became professor at Seoul National University in 2004.
Eunyoung Choe (born 1968) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Korea University. She held a post as an HK Professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2015).

Eva K. Neumaier (born 1937) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. In 2006, she was attested as Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary and as Professor Emeritus and former Department Chair at the University of Alberta.
Eva K. Neumaier-Dargyay (born 1937) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Rigzin and held an appointment at the University of Calgary.

Eva Tichy (born 1951) is a linguist and Indologist. She earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1974–1981), completed her habilitation at the University of Marburg (~1982–1989), and held the chair of Indo-European linguistics at the University of Freiburg (1993–2017).

Eva Wilden (born 1965) specializes in Indology. She completed her MA, doctorate, and habilitation at the University of Hamburg (~1986–2003), became a maître de conférences at the EFEO in 2003, and was appointed professor at the University of Hamburg in 2017.

Evan Thompson (born 1962) specializes in philosophy, studying at Amherst under Robert Thurman and at Toronto under Francisco Varela. His posts include Canada Research Chair at York (2002–2005) and professorships at the University of Toronto (2005) and University of British Columbia (2013).

Eviatar Shulman (born 1973) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1999–2008), where he held a post from 2009 and served as chairman of the Department of Comparative Religion (~2013).

Eyal Aviv works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned a PhD from Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil (attested 2008), and held a position at George Washington University in 2014.

F. B. J. Kuiper (1907–2003) specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Utrecht under Willem Caland and at Leiden under C. C. Uhlenbeck and Nicolaas van Wijk, later serving as professor of Sanskrit at Leiden (1939–1972).

Fa Qing works in Buddhist studies. He completed a dissertation at the University of Calgary, where he was supervised by Leslie S. Kawamura and Anthony W. Barber, and later taught Nirupam Chakma and Yong Hua.

Fabienne Jagou (born 1964) works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed a PhD under Pierre-Étienne Will at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (~1994–1999) and became a maître de conférences at the EFEO around 2001.

Fabio Rambelli (born 1963) specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Ca' Foscari University, Naples "L'Orientale", and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, later holding posts at Sapporo University (2001–2002) and UC Santa Barbara (~2009).

Fabrizia Baldissera (born 1946) is an Indologist who studied at the "Federigo Enriques" Department of Mathematics (1969–2004). She held positions at the University of Florence (~1998) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".
Fafang (1904–1951) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu. He served as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

Fang-kuei Li (1902–1987) worked in linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology, studying at Michigan and Chicago under Edward Sapir. He held research posts at Academia Sinica (1929, 1973) and taught at Yale, Harvard, the University of Washington (1949–1969), and Hawaii (1969–1974).
Faren is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at Lancaster University (until 2008). Faren served as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).
